questions.question: In a fresh R 4.3 session in which no package has been attached, a student runs `c(1, 4) %>% sum()` and then `c(1, 4) |> sum()`. What happens?
options: Both return `[1] 5`, since both pipes are part of base R from version 4.1.0 on.
`|>` stops with an error until a package is attached; `%>%` returns `[1] 5`.
`%>%` stops with `could not find function "%>%"`; `|>` returns `[1] 5`.
Both stop with an error until `library(tidyverse)` has been run in the session.

questions.question: In the R console, with the tidyverse attached and a tibble `d` that has a numeric column `v`, a chain is typed over two lines. Which split makes R stop with an error on the second line?
options: Line 1 `n <- d %>% pull(v)`, line 2 `%>% unique() %>% length()`
Line 1 `n <- d %>% pull(`, line 2 `v) %>% unique() %>% length()`

questions.question: For a vector `v` that contains repeated values, three versions count its different values: (A) `u <- unique(v); length(u)`, (B) `length(unique(v))` and (C) `v %>% unique() %>% length()`. Which statement about the three versions is correct?
options: All three give the same count; only A also creates the object `u`.
B runs `length()` first, as it is written first, so B returns `length(v)`.
C gives a larger count, as the pipe sends `v` to both `unique()` and `length()`.
Only A and C can be stored with `<-`; a nested call like B cannot be.

questions.question: For a numeric vector `v` with at least two values and no missing values, the chain `v %>% sort() %>% head(2) %>% sum()` is run. What does `sum()` receive as its first argument?
options: the whole vector `v`, as every step of a chain starts from `v`
the sorted vector `v`, as `head()` only prints its first two values
the first two elements of `v`, in their original order
the two smallest values of `v`, in increasing order

questions.question: With the tidyverse attached, what does `5 %>% paste("Total:")` return?
options: an error, because `paste()` already has an argument

questions.question: For a numeric vector `x`, which pipe chain computes the same as the nested call `sqrt(sum(abs(x)))`?
With the tidyverse attached and `d <- tibble(a = c(1, 2, 3))`, which line stops with an error in R 4.3?
With the tidyverse attached, a student runs `y <- c(1, 4, 9) %>% sqrt() %>% sum()`. What does `print(y)` show?
With the tidyverse attached and `d <- tibble(score = c(4, 8, 6))`, which chain returns `[1] 6`, the mean of the column `score`?
With the tidyverse attached and `d <- tibble(country = c("NL", "NL", "BE", "DE", "BE"), year = c(2020, 2020, 2020, 2020, 2021))`, which chain returns the number of different countries?

With the tidyverse attached and `d <- tibble(year = c(2019, 2020, 2021), emis = c(30, 22, 31))`, the chain `d %>% filter(emis > 25) %>% pull(emis)` works, but `d %>% pull(emis) %>% filter(emis > 25)` stops with an error. Why?
options: `pull()` returns a numeric vector, and `filter()` needs a table as its first argument.
dplyr verbs have a fixed order, and `filter()` must always come before `pull()`.
`pull()` removes the column `emis` from `d`, so `emis > 25` finds no such column.
`%>%` can pass on only tibbles, so nothing may follow a step that returns a vector.

questions.question: With the tidyverse attached and `sub <- function(x, k = 1) x - k`, what does `5 %>% sub() %>% sub(10)` return?
For a numeric vector `x` that may contain missing values, which pipe chain makes exactly the same computation as `round(mean(x, na.rm = TRUE), 2)`?

In the R console, with the tidyverse attached and `d <- tibble(v = c(2, 5, 7))`, a student types line 1 `total <- d %>% pull(v)` and then line 2 `%>% sum()`. Line 2 gives an `unexpected SPECIAL` error. What does `total` contain afterwards?
options: nothing, as the failed command was never run
the one-column tibble `v`, not a vector

questions.question: With the tidyverse attached, `d <- tibble(v = c(2, 5, 7))` and no object called `v` in the workspace, what does `d %>% sum(v)` return?
options: a tibble with one row in which `v` equals 14
an error, because R finds no object called `v`

questions.question: With the tidyverse attached, which pair of chains gives the same result for every numeric vector `x` with at least one element?
With the tidyverse attached and `x <- c(2, 3, 5)`, a student writes `x %>% sum(x)` to add up the values. What does it return?
With the tidyverse attached and `pw <- function(p, x) x^p`, what does `3 %>% pw(2)` return, and why?
options: `[1] 9`: the pipe sends 3 to the argument named `x`.
an error: 3 and 2 are both matched to `p`.
`[1] 9`: the written 2 fills `p` and the 3 fills what is left.

questions.question: With the tidyverse attached, what does `c(-2, 3) %>% sum(abs())` return?
options: an error, because `abs()` is called without an argument
`[1] 5`, the sum of the absolute values
`[1] 1`, the sum of the values as they are
`[1] 6`, the sum of the values and their absolute values
